claims.text: In-context learning has emerged as a groundbreaking ability of Large Language Models (LLMs).
In-context learning has revolutionized various fields.
In-context learning provides a few task-relevant demonstrations in the prompt.
Large Language Model responses face trustworthy issues such as hallucination.
Predictive uncertainty in in-context learning stems from provided demonstrations (aleatoric uncertainty).
Predictive uncertainty in in-context learning stems from ambiguities tied to the model's configurations (epistemic uncertainty).
The authors propose a novel formulation to quantify aleatoric and epistemic uncertainties in in-context learning.
The authors propose an estimation method to quantify aleatoric and epistemic uncertainties in in-context learning.
The proposed method offers an unsupervised way to understand the prediction of in-context learning.
The proposed method operates in a plug-and-play fashion.

methodologies.name: Unsupervised Uncertainty Decomposition for ICL
methodologies.description: A novel formulation and estimation method to quantify and decompose predictive uncertainty into aleatoric and epistemic components in an unsupervised, plug-and-play fashion.

limitations.text: Existing works often overlook the complex nature of LLMs in uncertainty quantification.
Existing works often overlook the uniqueness of in-context learning in uncertainty quantification.
